Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Abdullah Shafique and Fakhar Zaman are the two openers for Pakistan. Taskin Ahmed to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Pakistan showcased a dominant display in the first innings, demonstrating their mastery over the match's tempo right from the opening overs. They maintained a stranglehold on the game, consistently chipping away at the Bangladesh batting order with timely wickets. Apart from the resolute Mahmudullah, none of the Bangladesh batters seemed at ease at the crease, a testament to the effectiveness of the Pakistani bowlers. The ferocious Shaheen Afridi Afridi reached a significant milestone by claiming his 100th ODI wicket and went on to contribute three crucial scalps to his team's cause. Mohammad Wasim joined in the success with three wickets of his own, while Haris Rauf played his part with two vital breakthroughs. Pakistan's bowlers remained disciplined, exploiting the wicket's nuances and keeping the pressure mounted on the Bangladesh side throughout the innings. As the teams swap roles, Pakistan is now tasked with the challenge of chasing down a target of 205 runs in their allocated 50 overs, with the pitch continuing to offer ample opportunities to the bowlers. The question now looms large - Can they successfully navigate this pursuit, or will the Bangladeshi bowlers conjure a magic trick to alter the script? We await the unfolding drama in the coming innings.

Haris Rauf is down for a chat. He says that they bowled brilliantly and tried bowling wicket-to-wicket and sticking to their lengths on what was a slowish track. Mentions that there was certainly some reverse swing on offer and they tried to complement each other as a bowling unit. Mentions that Shaheen Afridi is all class and his wickets up top help the team a lot and when he performs, it gives them a lot of confidence.

Bangladesh embarked on their innings with the odds stacked against them, immediately facing a fiery spell from Pakistan's Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf. The opening overs saw Bangladesh's top order crumble, with the early wickets of three key batters tumbling within the first five overs. Litton Das and Mahmudullah, however, sought to steer the ship back on course and managed to orchestrate a spirited recovery, amassing a crucial 79-run partnership for the fourth wicket. The promising partnership took a blow when Litton Das surrendered his wicket to Iftikhar Ahmed, giving Pakistan a breath of fresh air. Despite the loss of his partner, Mahmudullah persisted, striking another impressive half-century with a composed 70-ball innings. His determined knock was eventually brought to an end by the relentless Shaheen Afridi in the 31st over. With Mahmudullah's departure, the bulk of Bangladesh's resistance crumbled, with Shakib Al Hasan being the only beacon of hope. However, his valiant 43-run effort was curtailed in the 40th over. Subsequently, Bangladesh's batting line-up fell like a house of cards, and the innings concluded in the 45th over, posting a total of 204 runs.

As the sun begins to set at the grand stage of the ICC Men's World Cup 2023, we mark the culmination of the first innings in Match No. 31, a contest between Pakistan and Bangladesh. The backdrop of the evening sky is illuminated with anticipation as we prepare to delve into the second half of this encounter. After a decisive toss, Bangladesh's leader, Shakib Al Hasan, chose to test the waters of batting first, seeking to post a competitive total. As the dust settles after 45 overs of intense cricketing action, Bangladesh has managed to muster a total of 204 runs on the board, leaving Pakistan with the task of scoring 205 runs for victory in their allotted 50 overs. The stage is set, and with a pitch offering ample opportunities for both the batsmen and bowlers, we eagerly await Pakistan's response as they step up to the crease.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to play! The umpires are out in the middle as the Pakistan team is seen in a huddle before striding out to the middle. Tanzid Hasan and Litton Das will open the innings for Bangladesh. Shaheen Afridi has the new ball in hand and will look to get some early purchase here. A couple of slips in place, let's go...

Just a few minutes left now for the game to get underway, but first, the two sets of players along with their mascots will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Bangladesh first, followed by the national anthem of Pakistan.

Pakistani speedster, Shaheen Afridi is down for a quick chat. On being on the cusp of 100 ODI wickets, he says that he still remembers his debut and to be so close to this achievement feels amazing. Adds that you win and lose as a team and they can only give it their all, the rest is not in their hands. Mentions that they still lost and will look to get over the line in the remaining games. Adds that there won't be much swing here and the length will be crucial and they were trying to bowl on a hard length in practice. On Mohammad Wasim, he says that early on he was erratic but has worked hard in the nets and it is good to see him get a chance to play.

The Pakistan skipper, Babar Azam says that they would have batted first as well because the wicket looks very dry but will now look to make good use of the early conditions. Adds that in the last game, they were good in all departments but failed to cross the line and will look to get the job done here. On not being able to convert fifties in hundreds, he says that he is also disappointed with that and will look to get to that three-figure mark. Adds that there are three changes in the team with Imam-ul-Haq, Mohammad Nawaz and Shadab Khan all missing out and Fakhar Zaman, Agha Salman and Usama Mir have replaced them.

Shakib Al Hasan, the captain of Bangladesh decides to bat first. Says that it looks like a dry wicket and they played on such a wicket a few days back and it starts to turn in the second half. He says that they don't have anything to lose from here on and will look to play better cricket. He also says that the culture here is pretty similar to back home and expects a good turnout of the crowd here at Kolkata and hopes to give them a good win tonight. Ends by informing that Mahedi Hasan is out and Towhid Hridoy comes in for him.

We have arrived at round 31 of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023. In this game, Pakistan will go up against Bangladesh at the Eden Gardens Stadium in Kolkata. Both teams are coming into this match riding on the back of recent losses. Bangladesh looked strong in their first match where they clinched a win over Afghanistan but it has been nothing but a series of losses for this team in the rest of their matches. Their last match was against the Netherlands where they failed to chase the target and lost by 87 runs. Their bowlers did a good job by restricting the Dutch to a low total of 229 with Shoriful Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, and Mahedi Hasan taking 2 wickets each. Shakib Al Hasan who was back with the team clinched one wicket to seal the innings. It was their batting unit that let them down. Litton Das and Tanzid Hasan both have them are both expected to give a strong start but they are not able to do so. Mehidy Hasan tried to stabilize the innings but he too was dismissed. None of the batters kept the partnership going and gave away their wickets to the opposition. They failed to perform under pressure which put them on a 5-match losing streak. This match is a good opportunity for them to gain some confidence towards the end of the league stages. Pakistan also started their campaign well by winning their opening two games against the Netherlands and Sri Lanka. After their loss against India, this team had to face a series of defeats. This Pakistani team carried a lot of expectations from their fans and the experts rated it as a team to be feared and capable of finishing in the top 4 on the points table but their performance hasn't been up to the mark. Their last game against South Africa was a nail-biter with the Proteas taking the win after fighting brutally. Pakistan put up a good score but the openers again failed to score big and got out early. It was the middle and lower order who helped to put up a competitive score on the board. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan put up a good stand with Saud Shakeel and Shadab Khan handling the innings in the later stages. Their bowling unit also managed to take timely wickets and didn't allow the opposition batters to score big except for Markram who changed the tide against Pakistan. Shaheen Afridi clinched three important wickets while Haris Rauf, Usama Mir, and Mohammad Wasim got two each. Mohammad Nawaz and Iftikhar Ahmed leaked some runs. The absence of a full-time spinner from the squad is turning out to be a great disadvantage for Pakistan as they are struggling in those middle overs. In the end, the Proteas managed to chase down the total with only a wicket left. It was a close match but Pakistan was on the losing end of it. This match is expected to be an exciting one as one of them will end their losing streak and get back to winning ways. This match is very crucial for Pakistan in order to have a chance to qualify for the semi-finals of the tournament. Which team are you supporting?
